# Voice annotator sidecar -- direct imports of voice_annotator.py only.
# Full setup, including the CUDA notes, is in README.md next to this file.
#
# Two things about this list are not obvious:
#
#   torch is used ONLY by silero-vad, to run a tiny VAD over 512-sample chunks.
#   Whisper does NOT go through torch -- faster-whisper runs it on CTranslate2,
#   which ships its own CUDA support. So a CPU-only torch build is enough here
#   even with --device cuda, and it saves a ~2.5 GB download.
#
#   torchaudio is pulled in by silero-vad rather than by this script. Listed
#   explicitly so an install that drops it fails here rather than at load time.

numpy
pyaudio
torch
torchaudio
silero-vad>=5.1
faster-whisper>=1.0

# ── GPU Whisper on Windows ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# device="cuda" with compute_type="int8_float16" needs the CUDA cuBLAS and cuDNN
# DLLs findable at import time. CTranslate2 does not bundle them. If
# WhisperModel(...) raises "Library cublas64_*.dll is not found" or
# "cudnn_ops_infer64_*.dll", uncomment these -- pip drops the DLLs into
# site-packages/nvidia/ where recent CTranslate2 finds them.
#
# nvidia-cublas-cu12
# nvidia-cudnn-cu12
#
# Or run CPU-only: python voice_annotator.py --device cpu
# small.en on CPU is a few hundred ms per short utterance, which is usable for
# annotation even if it is not what the 3090 is for.

# ── Freezing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Nothing above is pinned, because the working combination depends on the CUDA
# runtime on the machine and I would only be guessing. Once the env runs:
#
#     pip freeze > requirements.lock.txt
#
# and commit that. For the frozen collection campaign the lock file is what
# matters; this file is the recipe for building a new env from scratch.
